From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Aurum private cluster intake — inventory attached

James — thanks for the inventory. Uploaded and reviewed. High level checklist for a smooth on-prem private deploy (we'll use this for the SRE preflight):

1) Network & IAM
- Whitelist Redwood control-plane and SRE IPs for KMS and API callback ranges.
- Confirm whether outbound egress is NAT vs direct public; provide a small test route for a 5-minute connectivity check.
- VLAN allocation: need isolated VLAN(s) for control plane, workload, and management.

2) Cluster & OS
- K8s version target: 1.30.x or later (we can support 1.28+ but recommend 1.30).
- Base OS image and kernel: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, kernel 6.x preferred for GPU drivers.
- NTP and DNS resolvers reachable from nodes.

3) Node layout and storage guidance (proposed)
- Control plane: 3x control nodes (no GPU), small NVMe for etcd + journaling (120GB)
- Inference pool: 6x GPU nodes (A100/RTX-class as noted in inventory) with local NVMe + 1-2TB attached blockstore for model artifacts
- Node-decant (scratch) pool: 3x high-IO NVMe nodes acting as ingestion/decant tier — short-lived local storage for pre-processing, cache, and KV spill before commit to long-term block/object store

Why node-decant? For Aurum's bursty batch jobs, decant nodes reduce small-write pressure on the shared blockstore and reduce egress to object store by enabling short-term local aggregation. We'll propose an eviction policy and TTL (30-90 minutes) for decant volumes.

4) Storage classes & retention
- Local-ssd (fast ephemeral, used by decant pool)
- blockstore-encrypted (network-attached block store for model artifacts, backed by customer SAN)
- object-archive (for model checkpoints >30d)

5) Security / compliance
- KMS integration: will need sample encrypt/decrypt tests.
- Audit logging: we need access to syslog/S3-style audit sink (we can ingest via secure forwarder).

Next steps from Redwood:
- Ben will draft a node-pool sizing proposal and PV class mapping.
- We'll generate a short config template for your infra team to run a connectivity sanity check.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_requirements.pdf (contains our preflight checklist and driver matrix).

Can you confirm the KMS hostname and whether you permit IPs to reach it from our control-plane CIDR? Also please send a PDF or PNG of the network diagram rather than only Excel.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_onprem_requirements.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 21 Apr 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurum private cluster intake — inventory attached

Looping in a quick sizing idea based on the inventory and the decant concept:

- Node pools: control(3x m5-large), inference-gpu(6x p4/8/12 class), decant-io(3x r5d-style with 8TB NVMe).
- PV mapping: decant-io -> local-ssd (ephemeral), inference-gpu -> blockstore-encrypted (attach policy), control -> small persistent (etcd backups to object-archive).
- Decant policy: 30 minute TTL by default, automatic reconcile job to commit aggregates to blockstore every 10 mins; fallback to object-archive for oversized spill.
- Batching/burst: configure Redwood runtime to prefer local-kv cache on decant nodes for the first 100k tokens of a batch to reduce remote I/O.

Notes: with a single 10Gbps uplink, plan for off-peak bulk transfer windows or a direct physical link for object-sync. If Aurora (sic) wants <24h retention on decant, that will largely avoid egress spikes.

I'll prepare a short node-pool manifest and a PVclass matrix — target to send by Monday.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Platform Solutions, Redwood Inference
